source: Kimi K2.6 PP13 live startup telemetry on 2026-06-11 plus first-three PP8 Qwen/Gemma measured per-layer memory from profiles/production/first3_resident_memory_budget.json.

resident_batch_token_budget.notes: Kimi is raised from the boot-safe batch-4/8192-token profile to batch 16 with a 32768-token scheduler gate. This allows 16 active requests without permitting 16 fully-prefilling 8192-token requests in one step. Raise again only after live throughput and power telemetry prove office power margin.

kimi_batch16_fit_estimate.basis: Live Kimi-only startup reported roughly 48.14 GiB available GPU KV memory and 11905328 GPU KV tokens on rank0 at gpu_memory_utilization=0.70. The resident profile fixes Kimi KV to 8 GiB, roughly 16.6% of that allocation.
kimi_batch16_fit_estimate.notes: This is an order-of-magnitude fit check, not a substitute for a relaunch. It says max_num_seqs=16 should fit comfortably with the fixed 8 GiB Kimi KV cap; the practical constraints are power and scheduler workspace.

projection.notes: Projection subtracts Qwen and Gemma model-layer estimates plus 2 GiB/node local CPU LMCache allowance from live Kimi-only MemAvailable. It does not count GPU-power margin; enforce power first through batch limits and service concurrency until a hardware power cap is proven.

power_policy.hardware_power_limit_status: No reliable per-Spark 150W NVML/powercap limit was exposed by nvidia-smi or /sys/class/powercap during the 2026-06-11 probe.
power_policy.initial_control: Use DSAPI service batch limits, token budgets, and one-running-batch-per-compute-domain admission until a hardware power cap is proven. Kimi batch 16 is a throughput target, not permission to saturate all three resident services at once.

promotion_gates: Kimi 92-question COMPSEC run scores high enough to replace DSV4 as smart model.
